claims.body: Since 2023-24, Daccord has been a wall against the Blackhawks, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Blackhawks finally get to him.

story.head: The Kraken’s edge in preventing dangerous shots
paras: The Kraken (11-9-1) beat Anaheim 3-2 on Monday, and the Blackhawks have won two in a row. Going in, the Hawks are last in the Central (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Kraken fourth in the Pacific (tied for 22nd).
The Blackhawks’ record (.375) is about what their chances are worth. The Kraken’s record (.548) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.436), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Blackhawks pick their shots (lowest), rarely throw hits (2nd lowest) and don’t block many shots (31st). Chicago has allowed 3.96 goals a game, the second most in the league. The Kraken rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd), give up a lot of shots (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (31st). The Kraken have the edge over the Blackhawks on preventing dangerous shots.

Roman Kantserov (13 G / 5 A / 18 P in 24 GP) leads the Blackhawks in scoring. Patrick Kane (2 G / 15 A / 17 P in 21 GP) isn’t far behind, with eight points in his last five games. For the Kraken, Berkly Catton (8 G / 10 A / 18 P in 21 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Brandon Montour (3 G / 13 A / 16 P in 20 GP) isn’t far behind.

Spencer Knight (7-11-1 / .888 SV% in 19 GS) is expected to start for Chicago, and Joey Daccord (5-4-0 / .877 SV% in 10 GS) for Seattle. Daccord has a .934 save percentage in seven starts against the Blackhawks, well above his usual .903. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
